---
name: ai-sdk
description: 'Answer questions about the AI SDK and help build AI-powered features. Use when developers: (1) Ask about AI SDK functions like generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent, embed, or tools, (2) Want to build AI agents, chatbots, RAG systems, or text generation features, (3) Have questions about AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.), streaming, tool calling, structured output, or embeddings, (4) Use React hooks like useChat or useCompletion. Triggers on: "AI SDK", "Vercel AI SDK", "generateText", "streamText", "add AI to my app", "build an agent", "tool calling", "structured output", "useChat".'
---

## What the AI SDK Is

The AI SDK by Vercel (the `ai` package on npm) is a TypeScript toolkit for building AI applications. It provides a unified API across model providers for text generation, structured output, tool calling, agents, embeddings, and framework UI integrations.

- Repository: https://github.com/vercel/ai
- Documentation: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs

## Critical: Do Not Trust Your Own Memory

Whatever you remember about the AI SDK is likely outdated. The SDK changes frequently across versions - APIs are renamed, removed, and added. Your training data almost certainly contains obsolete APIs, deprecated patterns, and model IDs that no longer exist. UI hooks like `useChat` are among the most frequently changed APIs, so be especially careful with client code.

**Never write AI SDK code from memory.** Always verify every API, option, and pattern against the documentation and source code for the version that is actually installed in the project.

## Use the Bundled, Version-Matched Docs

The `ai` package ships its full documentation and source code inside `node_modules`. These always match the installed version, so trust them over anything you remember.

1. Ensure `ai` is installed. Check `node_modules/ai/` or locate the workspace package in a monorepo that depends on `ai` (e.g. `apps/<name>/node_modules/ai/`). If `ai` is not installed anywhere in the project, install **only** the `ai` package into the target package using the project's package manager (e.g. `pnpm add ai --filter <pkg>` or `npm install ai`). Install provider packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/openai`) and framework packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/react`) later, when the task requires them.
2. Read and grep the bundled docs at `node_modules/ai/docs/` (or `<package>/node_modules/ai/docs/`) and the source at `node_modules/ai/src/`.
3. Provider and framework packages bundle their own docs at `node_modules/@ai-sdk/<name>/docs/` (or `<package>/node_modules/@ai-sdk/<name>/docs/`).
4. If something isn't in the bundled docs, search https://ai-sdk.dev/docs. You can append `.md` to any docs page URL to get its markdown, and search via `https://ai-sdk.dev/api/search-docs?q=your_query`.
5. If you cannot find support for an answer in the docs or source, say so explicitly — do not guess.

## AI Gateway: The Fastest Way to Start

The Vercel AI Gateway is the fastest way to get started with the AI SDK. It provides access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other providers through a single API, without installing provider packages or managing multiple API keys.

To set it up:

1. Authenticate with OIDC (for Vercel deployments) or get an AI Gateway API key.
2. Provide it to your app via the `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` environment variable.
3. Reference models with `provider/model` strings.

For exact setup, authentication, and usage, read the bundled guide and the AI Gateway docs.

### Choosing a Model

Never use model IDs from memory — models are released and retired frequently. Fetch the current list before writing code that references a model. Do not truncate the list (e.g. with `head`) so you can find the newest models:

```bash
# All available models
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '.data[].id'

# Filter by provider (e.g. anthropic, openai, google)
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.id | startswith("anthropic/")) | .id] | reverse | .[]'
```

When multiple versions of a model exist, prefer the one with the highest version number.

## Building and Consuming Agents

Use the SDK's built-in agent abstraction (such as `ToolLoopAgent`) rather than hand-rolling tool-calling loops. For end-to-end type safety, infer the UI message type from your agent definition when consuming it on the client (e.g. with `useChat`). Consuming an agent is framework-specific: check `package.json` to detect the stack, then follow the matching quickstart.

Look up the current agent, tool, and type-safety APIs in the bundled docs (`node_modules/ai/docs/`, especially the agents section) or at https://ai-sdk.dev/docs.

## DevTools

AI SDK DevTools captures your AI SDK calls - requests, responses, tool calls, token usage, and multi-step runs - so you can inspect exactly what your agents do. Use it while developing to debug generations. It is a separate package and is intended for local development only.

For setup instructions, read the bundled DevTools documentation.

## Keep the SDK Current

Outdated installs are the most common source of errors. Compare the installed version against the latest:

- **Installed:** the `version` field in `node_modules/ai/package.json`.
- **Latest:** run `npm view ai version`.

lines: -# Chiri Engineering Assessment — AI Document Editor
-## The Challenge

-Build a collaborative AI document editor in the browser. The user writes Markdown, and an AI agent works alongside them — suggesting edits, showing diffs, and iterating on the document together. Don't build a full markdown editor from scratch, a prebuilt like tiptap or similar is fine.

-Think Google Docs meets AI pair-writing. The user is always in control, but the AI is a capable collaborator that can rewrite paragraphs, fix tone, restructure sections, or follow specific instructions.
-## What to Build
-A single page web app, no auth required, where:
-1. The user can write and edit Markdown in a browser-based editor
-2. An AI agent can suggest changes to the document (or a selection)
-3. Suggestions appear as visible diffs — the user can see exactly what the AI wants to change before accepting
-4. The user can accept, reject, or refine the AI's suggestions
-5. The experience feels collaborative — like working with a smart co-author, not a chatbot in a sidebar and not something that completes the whole document
-Beyond that, the design is yours. We're intentionally leaving this open and how you interpret "collaborative editing with AI" tells us a lot.
-## What We Provide
-- An OpenRouter API key with a $5 spending cap — use any model available through OpenRouter
-- That's it. The rest is up to you.
-## What to Submit
-1. Host your code on GitHub or GitLab and send us the link
-2. Include a README with: how to run it, what you built, and what you'd do differently with more time

-3. Save your AI session(s) — we want to see how you used AI to build this. Send the raw, unedited session files exactly as your tool saved them (for example, Claude Code `.jsonl` files from `~/.claude/projects/`, a Cursor composer history export, or the official data export file of ChatGPT or Claude.ai). We accept files only, not share links. Do not edit, summarize, translate or reformat them, and do not write or generate a session log after the work. The only change allowed is to mask secrets such as API keys. You can work with the AI in the language you prefer. This is not optional, please commit the files to the git repository along with the project code.
-## What We Evaluate
-| What matters | What we look for |
-| The experience | Is it intuitive? Can we open it, write something, and get useful AI suggestions without reading docs? |
-| AI integration quality | Does the agent feel like a collaborator or a gimmick? Are diffs clear and useful? |
-| How you used AI to build it | Did you use AI tools effectively to ship faster? Can you explain the choices made? |
-| Code quality | Is the code organized, readable, and something a teammate could pick up? |
-| Taste & judgment | What did you prioritize? What did you intentionally leave out? Trade-offs matter more than features. |
-## What We Don't Care About
-- Docker, databases, auth systems — don't add infrastructure you don't need, this is just a showcase of a simple app so we can judge AI usage
-- Visual perfection — but it should be usable and not broken
-- Using a specific framework — React, Vue, Svelte, vanilla JS, whatever you're fast with
-## Guidelines
-**Time:** Spend what feels right. This is meant to be fun, not a grind. A focused 4-6 hour session beats a sprawling weekend project.
-**AI usage is required, not just encouraged.** We use AI every day in our engineering workflow. Show us how you work with it:
-- Use Claude, Cursor, Copilot, ChatGPT, or any AI tool to build this
-- Save the raw, unedited session/transcript — we'll review it alongside the code
-## Ideas (not requirements)
-These are just sparks if you want them. Build whatever version of this excites you:
-- Inline suggestions that appear as tracked changes
-- A command palette or slash commands for AI actions
-- Split-pane diff view (before/after)
-- "Rewrite this section in a different tone" with live preview
-- Version history showing how the document evolved with AI help
-- Multi-turn refinement — "make it shorter," "now more formal," "add examples"

# AGENTS.md

Browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. The AI proposes inline, reviewable suggestions; the user accepts, rejects, or refines them. Built for the [Chiri assessment](docs/chiri/CHALLENGE.md).

## Read first

1. [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md) — use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues.
2. [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) — slices, roles, gates, the per-slice loop.
3. The GitHub issue you are working on, and every ADR it links in [docs/chiri/adr/](docs/chiri/adr/).

ADRs are decisions, not suggestions. If an ADR blocks you, stop and report it; do not work around it.

## Stack

| Concern | Choice |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node 22+ (required by `ai@7`) |
| Package manager | pnpm (pin with `packageManager` in `package.json`) |
| App | Vite + React + TypeScript (strict) |
| Editor | CodeMirror 6, `@codemirror/lang-markdown` |
| Styling | Tailwind v4, theme tokens in CSS via `@theme`; dark theme only; sans-serif; League Spartan for the app title |
| AI | `ai@^7` + `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@^3` + `zod` |
| Diff | `diff` (jsdiff) |
| Tests | Vitest |
| Lint/format | Biome |

Commands (once slice 1 lands): `pnpm dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm biome check`, `pnpm build`. Slice 2 adds `pnpm bakeoff`.

## AI SDK

- Follow [.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk/SKILL.md) (copied verbatim from `vercel/ai@c739d37`, `skills/use-ai-sdk/`). **Never write AI SDK code from memory**: read `node_modules/ai/docs/` and the provider's bundled docs first.
- Ignore the skill's AI Gateway section. This project calls OpenRouter through the Vite proxy ([ADR 0005](docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
- Model IDs come from `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`, never from memory.

## Code style

- Functional: pure functions, immutable data, no classes unless a library demands one.
- No comments unless strictly necessary.
- English everywhere: identifiers, files, logs, errors, tests, commits, PRs, issues. UI copy is English too.
- Suggested layout; refine it if the code asks for it, and say so in the PR:

```text
src/
├── editor/        # CodeMirror setup, decorations, keymaps
├── suggestions/   # Suggestion state, lifecycle, position mapping (pure)
├── diff/          # adaptive diff (pure)
├── blocks/        # Block extraction from the syntax tree (pure)
├── ai/            # model client, zod schemas, prompt building, AI call records
└── ui/            # React components
scripts/
└── bakeoff.ts
```

## Tests

- TDD (red → green → refactor) for pure modules: diff → hunks, Suggestion state and position mapping, Block extraction, prompt building, schema validation, AI call records.
- No E2E suite. UI is verified in a real browser with the `agent-browser` skill.
- Tests never call the real model.

## Git and PRs

- One branch per issue, from `main`: `feat/ | fix/ | chore/ | refactor/ | docs/ | test/` + short kebab slug, max 40 chars.
- Commit messages: short, imperative, conventional prefix. No `Co-Authored-By` or other authorship trailers.
- PR body: use the `pr` skill, filling [.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Start with `Closes #N`.
- Squash merge only.

## Definition of done (every slice)

1. `pnpm test` green, with TDD on the pure modules the issue lists.
2. `pnpm biome check` clean and `pnpm build` green.
3. The issue's acceptance criteria checked in a real browser with `agent-browser`.
4. AI calls made during that check recorded (next section), with screenshots.
5. Code review done and real findings fixed (roles in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)).
6. PR opened from the template, then squash-merged.

## AI call records

Every check that calls the model is recorded. This is how the US$5 budget is accounted for.

- In dev mode, the model client appends one record per call to `window.__aiCalls`. It is fed by a custom `registerTelemetry` integration (no OpenTelemetry) and enriched with `GET /api/v1/generation?id=…` through the proxy.
- After a check, read the log with `agent-browser` (`eval`).
- Fields: task requested (e.g. "select paragraph 2 → Shorter"), model requested, model and provider that served it, tokens (input / output / reasoning / cached), cost, latency (client total, OpenRouter `latency`, `generation_time`, time to first Suggestion for review passes), `finish_reason`, valid or retried, generation `id`.
- Where:
  - `docs/chiri/verification/<issue>-<slug>.md`: the full table plus screenshots for that slice.
  - `docs/chiri/verification/img/<issue>-<n>.png`: screenshots, committed. Link them in the PR by commit SHA so links survive branch deletion.
  - [docs/chiri/ai-costs.md](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md): one row per check, plus the running total against the US$5 cap.
  - PR: a summary table under Evidence.

## Secrets

- The key lives only in `.env` (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). Never commit it, print it, or put it in the bundle.
- The browser sends a placeholder key; the Vite proxy overwrites `Authorization`.

## Gates

The orchestrator stops and waits for the maintainer at the gates in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md). Never skip a gate.

# Glossary

Use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues. Avoid synonyms such as "edit", "proposal" or "patch" for a Suggestion.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Document** | The Markdown text in the editor. The only thing the app persists (`localStorage`). |
| **Block** | A top-level node of the CodeMirror Markdown syntax tree: paragraph, heading, list, blockquote, code block. A whole list is one Block. |
| **Target** | The range an AI request is about: the selection, or the Block under the cursor when nothing is selected. |
| **Neighbors** | The 2 Blocks before and the 2 after the Target, plus the document title (first `#`) and the current section heading. Sent as context. |
| **Instruction** | What the user asks for: a Quick action or free text. |
| **Quick action** | A preset Instruction: Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar. |
| **Suggestion** | A proposed replacement for a range of the Document. It lives outside the Document (an overlay) until accepted. Holds: range, original text, Replacement, Rationale, refine history. |
| **Replacement** | The new text the AI proposes for a Suggestion's range. |
| **Rationale** | One short sentence from the AI explaining the change, in the Document's language. Shown on hover, or when the cursor is inside the Suggestion. |
| **Active Suggestion** | The most recently created Suggestion, or the one containing the cursor. The only one that shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. |

# AGENTS.md

Browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. The AI proposes inline, reviewable suggestions; the user accepts, rejects, or refines them. Built for the [Chiri assessment](docs/chiri/CHALLENGE.md).

## Read first

1. [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md) — use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues.
2. [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) — slices, roles, gates, the per-slice loop.
3. The GitHub issue you are working on, and every ADR it links in [docs/chiri/adr/](docs/chiri/adr/).

ADRs are decisions, not suggestions. If an ADR blocks you, stop and report it; do not work around it.

## Stack

| Concern | Choice |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node 22+ (required by `ai@7`) |
| Package manager | pnpm (pin with `packageManager` in `package.json`) |
| App | Vite + React + TypeScript (strict) |
| Editor | CodeMirror 6, `@codemirror/lang-markdown` |
| Styling | Tailwind v4, theme tokens in CSS via `@theme`; dark theme only; sans-serif; League Spartan for the app title |
| AI | `ai@^7` + `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@^3` + `zod` |
| Diff | `diff` (jsdiff) |
| Tests | Vitest |
| Lint/format | Biome |

Commands (once slice 1 lands): `pnpm dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm biome check`, `pnpm build`. Slice 2 adds `pnpm bakeoff`.

## AI SDK

- Follow [.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk/SKILL.md) (copied verbatim from `vercel/ai@c739d37`, `skills/use-ai-sdk/`). **Never write AI SDK code from memory**: read `node_modules/ai/docs/` and the provider's bundled docs first.
- Ignore the skill's AI Gateway section. This project calls OpenRouter through the Vite proxy ([ADR 0005](docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
- Model IDs come from `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`, never from memory.

## Code style

- Functional: pure functions, immutable data, no classes unless a library demands one.
- No comments unless strictly necessary.
- English everywhere: identifiers, files, logs, errors, tests, commits, PRs, issues. UI copy is English too.
- Suggested layout; refine it if the code asks for it, and say so in the PR:

```text
src/
├── editor/        # CodeMirror setup, decorations, keymaps
├── suggestions/   # Suggestion state, lifecycle, position mapping (pure)
├── diff/          # adaptive diff (pure)
├── blocks/        # Block extraction from the syntax tree (pure)
├── ai/            # model client, zod schemas, prompt building, AI call records
└── ui/            # React components
scripts/
└── bakeoff.ts
```

## Tests

- TDD (red → green → refactor) for pure modules: diff → hunks, Suggestion state and position mapping, Block extraction, prompt building, schema validation, AI call records.
- No E2E suite. UI is verified in a real browser with the `agent-browser` skill.
- Tests never call the real model.

## Git and PRs

- One branch per issue, from `main`: `feat/ | fix/ | chore/ | refactor/ | docs/ | test/` + short kebab slug, max 40 chars.
- Commit messages: short, imperative, conventional prefix. No `Co-Authored-By` or other authorship trailers.
- PR body: use the `pr` skill, filling [.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Start with `Closes #N`.
- Squash merge only.

## Definition of done (every slice)

1. `pnpm test` green, with TDD on the pure modules the issue lists.
2. `pnpm biome check` clean and `pnpm build` green.
3. The issue's acceptance criteria checked in a real browser with `agent-browser`.
4. AI calls made during that check recorded (next section), with screenshots.
5. Code review done and real findings fixed (roles in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)).
6. PR opened from the template, then squash-merged.

## AI call records

Every check that calls the model is recorded. This is how the US$5 budget is accounted for.

- In dev mode, the model client appends one record per call to `window.__aiCalls`. It is fed by a custom `registerTelemetry` integration (no OpenTelemetry) and enriched with `GET /api/v1/generation?id=…` through the proxy.
- After a check, read the log with `agent-browser` (`eval`).
- Fields: task requested (e.g. "select paragraph 2 → Shorter"), model requested, model and provider that served it, tokens (input / output / reasoning / cached), cost, latency (client total, OpenRouter `latency`, `generation_time`, time to first Suggestion for review passes), `finish_reason`, valid or retried, generation `id`.
- Where:
  - `docs/chiri/verification/<issue>-<slug>.md`: the full table plus screenshots for that slice.
  - `docs/chiri/verification/img/<issue>-<n>.png`: screenshots, committed. Link them in the PR by commit SHA so links survive branch deletion.
  - [docs/chiri/ai-costs.md](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md): one row per check, plus the running total against the US$5 cap.
  - PR: a summary table under Evidence.

## Secrets

- The key lives only in `.env` (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). Never commit it, print it, or put it in the bundle.
- The browser sends a placeholder key; the Vite proxy overwrites `Authorization`.

## Gates

The orchestrator stops and waits for the maintainer at the gates in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md). Never skip a gate.

# 0001. Inline Suggestions as an overlay on a raw-Markdown CodeMirror editor

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q1, Q2, Q9

## Context

The challenge asks for visible diffs before the user accepts, and for an experience that feels like a co-author, "not a chatbot in a sidebar". We had to choose where Suggestions appear and what kind of editor holds the text.

## Decision

- **Editor:** CodeMirror 6 showing raw Markdown with light styling, Obsidian-like: bigger headings, bold looks bold, syntax marks stay visible.
- **Suggestions inline, as tracked changes:** deleted text is struck through in place and the Replacement shows next to it, rendered with CodeMirror decorations and widgets.
- **Overlay, not content:** Suggestions live in editor state outside the Document. The Document only ever holds the user's text. Accept applies the Replacement as a normal edit. Reject drops the Suggestion.

## Consequences

- The Document is a plain string, so diffs are plain string diffs: simple and reliable.
- Copying, saving and persisting never leak Suggestion markup.
- The Replacement is not directly editable. Users Refine it, or Accept and then edit.
- Less "Google Docs" polish than a WYSIWYG editor.

## Alternatives considered

- **Split pane before/after:** easier, but the eye jumps between two places and it feels like a tool, not a partner.
- **Chat sidebar producing patches:** what the challenge says to avoid.
- **Tiptap / ProseMirror WYSIWYG:** the Markdown round-trip is lossy, and tracked changes over a node tree are notoriously hard.
- **Suggestion text inserted into the Document with marks:** the Markdown stays dirty while Suggestions are open, and Reject needs careful undo.

# 0002. Structured model output; the app owns the anchors

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q10, Q39

## Context

What can go wrong with a model's answer here:

| Failure | Plain text | Structured JSON |
|---|---|---|
| Wrapper chatter ("Sure! Here's…", code fences) | happens, needs cleaning | gone, the schema enforces the shape |
| Changes beyond the Instruction | happens | happens equally |
| Invented content | happens | happens equally |
| Wrong location (quotes text that doesn't exist) | impossible, the app knows the range | **new risk**, if the model picks the location |

The diff itself guards against rows 2 and 3: every change is visible before Accept. Structure removes row 1 and makes the answer checkable, but can create row 4.

## Decision

- **Strict structured outputs:** `structured_outputs` with OpenRouter `provider.require_parameters: true`, so only providers that support it are used. One zod schema per shape is both the validator and the source of the JSON Schema.
- **Target requests and Refine:** the app already knows the range. The model returns `{ replacement, rationale }`.
- **Review pass:** the app numbers Blocks (`p1`, `p2`, …) before sending. The model returns `{ edits: [{ blockId, replacement, rationale }] }` and never copies text to say where. A Block is a top-level node of the Markdown syntax tree; a whole list is one Block.
- **App-side validation:** drop an item when `replacement` equals the original or `blockId` is unknown. On invalid output, retry once silently, then show an error card.

## Consequences

- No chatter, a Rationale for every change, and answers the app can check.
- Review pass granularity is one Block: two changes in one paragraph become one Suggestion, and a long list is a single Suggestion.
- Format constraints may slightly lower writing quality ("Let Me Speak Freely?", 2024). The Bake-off watches for it ([0010](0010-model-bakeoff.md)).

## Alternatives considered

- **Plain-text Replacement for Target requests:** simplest, but no Rationale and no validation.
- **Quote-anchored edits `{ quote, replacement }` everywhere:** uniform, but a one-character slip in `quote` drops the edit, even where the app already knew the range.
- **Character offsets:** models are bad at counting characters.
- **Blank-line splitting for Blocks:** breaks on lists without blank lines and on code blocks that contain empty lines.

# 0003. Adaptive diff granularity

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q11

## Context

Word-level diffs are perfect for small fixes and unreadable "confetti" for rewrites. Block-level diffs are clear for rewrites and hide one-word fixes.

## Decision

Diff the original against the Replacement word by word (`diff`, `diffWords`). If the share of changed words exceeds a threshold (start at ~40%, calibrate on the sample Document), render block-level instead: the whole original struck through, the Replacement below it.

## Consequences

- Readable for both small fixes and rewrites.
- One threshold to tune, kept as a named constant with tests on both sides of it.

## Alternatives considered

- Always word-level.
- Always block-level.

# 0004. User-triggered AI, plus an on-demand Review pass

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q5, Q12, Q28

## Context

"The user is always in control", but the AI should feel like a co-author, not something that completes the whole Document.

## Decision

- **The AI acts only when asked.**
- **Selection bubble:** Quick actions (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar) plus a free-text "Ask AI…" field. `Cmd/Ctrl+K` opens the same field. With no selection, the Target is the Block under the cursor.
- **Review pass:** a toolbar button with an optional Focus. Without Focus, the AI looks at clarity, concision, grammar and tone consistency. It returns at most 6 Suggestions, most important first. It skips code blocks and Blocks that already have an open Suggestion.
- **No slash commands, no proactive hints.**
- Many Suggestions can be open at once from day one.

## Consequences

- Predictable, cheap, and the user is in control.
- The Review pass gives the "colleague marking up my draft" feeling without ambient noise.
- The 6-Suggestion cap leaves issues untouched in long, rough Documents. A wall of red and green would read as "the AI rewrote everything".

## Alternatives considered

- **Proactive hints on idle:** the strongest co-author feel, but it burns tokens under a US$5 cap, is noisy, and is hard to tune.
- **Slash commands:** they pull toward "generate at cursor", which is close to completing the Document.
- **Free-text only, no Quick actions:** less discoverable. Reviewers would have to invent what to ask.

# 0005. Local-only app; API key behind the Vite dev proxy

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q4, Q8, Q22

## Context

The challenge asks for "how to run it" and says no infrastructure is needed. The OpenRouter key has a US$5 cap and must not reach the browser.

## Decision

- **Run locally only:** `pnpm dev`. No deploy.
- **Proxy:** Vite `server.proxy` (and `preview.proxy`) forwards `/api/openrouter/*` to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` and overwrites `Authorization` with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from `.env`. The browser sends a placeholder key.
- **Missing-key banner:** `vite.config` exposes only a boolean, `__HAS_OPENROUTER_KEY__`, never the key. Without a key, a fixed banner explains what to set.
- **Config:** `.env.example` lists `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and an optional `OPENROUTER_MODEL`.

## Consequences

- No extra process to run, and the key never reaches the bundle.
- Prompts live in client code. They are not secret.
- Deploying later means replacing the proxy with a serverless function.

## Alternatives considered

- **Public deploy:** reviewers click a link, but anyone could spend the US$5, and it needs rate limiting and infrastructure.
- **Small Hono server with `/api/suggest`:** a second process and more code.
- **Key in the bundle (`VITE_OPENROUTER_KEY`):** leaks the key.

# 0006. Context window and prompt rules

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q18, Q26, Q27

## Context

A rewrite that ignores the surrounding tone feels pasted in. Sending the whole Document on every request costs more and invites the model to wander.

## Decision

- **Target requests and Refine:** send the Target, its Neighbors (2 Blocks before, 2 after, the document title and the current section heading, ~300–800 tokens), and the Instruction. Refine also sends the original text, previous Instructions and the latest Replacement.
- **Review pass:** send the whole Document with numbered Blocks (it must choose where to act).
- **Fixed prompt rules:**
  1. Answer in the Target's language.
  2. Change only what the Instruction needs.
  3. Do not invent facts, numbers or names.
  4. Preserve Markdown syntax (lists, links, emphasis).
  5. Rationale: one short sentence, in the Document's language.
- **Reasoning:** off or low for Quick actions, where the model allows it.

## Consequences

- Cheaper than sending the whole Document, and the Neighbors carry the tone.
- The model can miss consistency issues outside the Neighbors. That is what the Review pass is for.
- Rule 2 makes the AI timid on open Instructions like "make this better". Free text still allows big changes when the user asks for them.

## Alternatives considered

- **Target only:** cheapest, but blind to tone and topic.
- **Whole Document on every request:** best tone match, but more tokens. A size limit for huge Documents would also be needed (backlog).

# 0007. Suggestion lifecycle

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q13, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q25, Q32

## Context

Suggestions are overlays ([0001](0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md)) and the user keeps typing while they are open or in flight.

## Decision

- **Edits outside a Suggestion:** its range is mapped through the change (CodeMirror `ChangeSet` mapping).
- **Edits inside an open Suggestion, or inside an in-flight request's Target:** Discard it, with a discreet notice ("Suggestion discarded: the text changed").
- **Overlaps:** a new request over an open Suggestion replaces it, so the last one wins. The Review pass skips Blocks with open Suggestions.
- **Active Suggestion:** shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. Its Rationale shows on hover, and when the text cursor is inside it (keyboard users can't hover). Other Suggestions show only the inline diff.
- **Keys, with the cursor inside a Suggestion:** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` Accepts, `Esc` Rejects. Accept is a normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. Reject is not undoable in v1. A Review pass also offers Accept all and Reject all.
- **Refine:** a follow-up Instruction on the Active Suggestion. The new Replacement replaces the old one in place. The diff is always against the original text. History stays in memory, with no version arrows in v1.
- **Persistence:** only the Document text goes to `localStorage`. Open Suggestions are lost on reload.
- **Failures:**
  - Missing key: banner ([0005](0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
  - Failed call (network, `402` out of credit, `429`): the Suggestion becomes an error card with Retry. `402` gets its own message.
  - Invalid output: one silent retry, then the error card.
  - Timeout: 30 s.

## Consequences

- Simple, honest rules. A user who bumps into a Suggestion loses it, and can ask again.
- An accidental `Esc` loses a Suggestion. An undoable Reject is in the backlog.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep a stale Suggestion with "regenerate":** an extra state, and an old diff can't be drawn over changed text.
- **Lock the range while a Suggestion is open:** takes control away from the user.
- **Block new requests until the old Suggestion is resolved:** friction.
- **Allow overlapping Suggestions:** accepting one breaks the other.
- **Rationale always visible, or in a side panel:** the side panel drifts toward the chatbot sidebar.

# 0008. Stream only where each piece arrives validated

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q24, Q31

## Context

Streaming has three costs here: parsing half-finished JSON, a diff that jitters while text arrives (not-yet-rewritten original text shows as deleted), and showing text before it is validated.

AI SDK v7, verified in its docs on 2026-10-28:
- With `Output.object`, `partialOutputStream` yields partial objects that "cannot be validated against your provided schema". Only the final output is validated.
- With `Output.array`, `elementStream` yields each element "complete and validated against your element schema".

## Decision

- **Review pass:** stream with `Output.array` and `elementStream`. Each Suggestion appears once it is schema-validated by the SDK and checked by the app (`blockId` exists, Replacement differs from the original).
- **Target requests and Refine:** not streamed. `Output.object`, validated before anything is shown.
- **Reopen rule:** if the chosen model's median latency for Target requests is above ~3 s, add a Draft preview: streamed text without a diff that turns into the diff once validated.

## Consequences

- The slowest call, the Review pass, shows its first Suggestion early, with no validation trade-off.
- Target requests stay simple: one state, validated before display.
- The Draft preview sits in the backlog behind a measurable rule.

## Alternatives considered

- **No streaming at all:** simplest, but the Review pass waits for all 6 Suggestions.
- **Stream everything, including a Draft for Target requests:** matches the challenge's "live preview" idea, but adds a visual state and a Draft that can fail validation and vanish.

# 0009. AI SDK v7 instead of plain fetch

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q31 (web-verified on 2026-10-28)

## Context

Without streaming, plain `fetch` + zod was ~60–80 lines and fully transparent. With validated element streaming ([0008](0008-validated-streaming-only.md)) and per-call records ([AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md#ai-call-records)), the SDK pays for itself.

Facts at decision time:
- `ai@7.0.155` (7.0.0 released 2026-06-25) and `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@3.1.0`, which targets `ai@^7`. Both are ESM-only and require Node 22+.
- Telemetry in v7 is a pluggable integration (`registerTelemetry`). A custom integration receives lifecycle events (`onStart`, `onStepEnd` with `usage`, `onEnd`, …) without OpenTelemetry.
- Every OpenRouter response includes `usage` with `cost`, reasoning tokens and cached tokens. `GET /api/v1/generation?id=…` adds `latency`, `generation_time`, `provider_name`, native token counts and more.

## Decision

- Use `ai@^7` + `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@^3` + `zod`.
- The provider uses `baseURL` = `${location.origin}/api/openrouter` and a placeholder key. The proxy injects the real key.
- AI call records come from a custom `registerTelemetry` integration plus the generation endpoint.
- `scripts/bakeoff.ts` uses the same client in Node with the real key, so the Bake-off tests the code the app runs.
- Agents follow `.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk` and never write SDK code from memory.

## Consequences

- Element streaming with validation, lifecycle hooks for records, and a cheap path to Draft streaming later.
- Two more dependencies. Node 22+ goes in the README.
- Official recipes run the SDK on a server. We run it in the browser. The core uses `fetch`, and a Chrome article shows `streamText()` working in the browser.
- **Risk:** the provider README does not document `Output.object` or `json_schema`. Slice 2 must verify this. The fallback is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (not yet verified).

## Alternatives considered

- **Plain `fetch` + zod:** smallest and transparent, but no validated element streaming.
- **OpenTelemetry export:** from the browser it needs a vendor key in the bundle, or a server.
- **AI SDK DevTools:** stores data in a local JSON file, so it only works in Node. Usable for the Bake-off only.

# 0010. Choose the model by Bake-off

- Status: **Proposed**. Decided at Gate A ([docs/PLAN.md](../../PLAN.md#gates)).
- Source: planning session, Q23, Q33

## Context

On 2026-10-28, from OpenRouter's public API. Prices are US$ per million tokens. Cost per call assumes ~3k input and ~500 output tokens (a Review pass).

| Tier | Model | Origin | Input | Output | ~Cost/call | Providers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cheap | `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | US | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.0006 | 10 |
| Cheap | `openai/gpt-6-luna` | US | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.0006 | 7 |
| Cheap | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | CN | 0.14 | 0.42 | 0.0006 | 41 |
| Cheap | `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.50 | 0.0007 | 38 |
| Cheap | `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.47 | 0.0007 | 2 |
| Cheap | `minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.60 | 0.0008 | 13 |
| Cheap | `z-ai/glm-5.3` | CN | 0.07 | 1.40 | 0.0009 | 49 |
| Mid | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | US | 0.30 | 2.50 | 0.002 | 8 |
| Mid | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` | CN | 0.66 | 1.98 | 0.003 | 25 |
| Mid | `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | US | 0.83 | 4.13 | 0.005 | 7 |
| Mid | `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` | US | 1 | 5 | 0.006 | 4 |
| Top | `qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902` | CN | 2 | 6 | 0.009 | 2 |
| Top | `google/gemini-4-argon` | US | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 6 |
| Top | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` | US | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 8 |
| Top | `moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro` | CN | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 2 |

Notes:
- Every model listed supports `structured_outputs` on at least some providers (`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`: 32 of 38). `z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-prime` were excluded because they don't support it.
- Open-weight models are served by many providers with different quantization, so quality and latency depend on who serves the call. Pinning a provider trades away automatic fallback.
- OpenRouter's API returns `latency_last_30m: null`, so there is no speed data up front.
- Most of these models were released after the planning model's training data. Choosing from this table alone would be choosing by brand and price.

## Decision

`scripts/bakeoff.ts` runs the same requests against 9 models:

`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `google/gemini-3.8-flash`, `google/gemini-4-argon`, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

- **Requests:** the 4 Quick actions on fixed Targets of the sample Document, plus 1 Review pass.
- **Measured:** latency, cost, schema validity and retries, plus the outputs side by side. Written to `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`.
- **Choice:** the maintainer picks by reading the outputs. Tie-breakers, in order: Target-request latency under ~3 s, then cost. The result may be two models: a fast one for Target requests and a strong one for the Review pass.
- **Default:** configurable via `OPENROUTER_MODEL`.
- **Budget:** under US$0.50.

## Consequences

- The choice rests on evidence, not on a guess.
- About 30–40 minutes of work, plus a Gate.
- The Bake-off also verifies the `Output.object` risk from [0009](0009-ai-sdk-v7.md).

# 0001. Inline Suggestions as an overlay on a raw-Markdown CodeMirror editor

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q1, Q2, Q9

## Context

The challenge asks for visible diffs before the user accepts, and for an experience that feels like a co-author, "not a chatbot in a sidebar". We had to choose where Suggestions appear and what kind of editor holds the text.

## Decision

- **Editor:** CodeMirror 6 showing raw Markdown with light styling, Obsidian-like: bigger headings, bold looks bold, syntax marks stay visible.
- **Suggestions inline, as tracked changes:** deleted text is struck through in place and the Replacement shows next to it, rendered with CodeMirror decorations and widgets.
- **Overlay, not content:** Suggestions live in editor state outside the Document. The Document only ever holds the user's text. Accept applies the Replacement as a normal edit. Reject drops the Suggestion.

## Consequences

- The Document is a plain string, so diffs are plain string diffs: simple and reliable.
- Copying, saving and persisting never leak Suggestion markup.
- The Replacement is not directly editable. Users Refine it, or Accept and then edit.
- Less "Google Docs" polish than a WYSIWYG editor.

## Alternatives considered

- **Split pane before/after:** easier, but the eye jumps between two places and it feels like a tool, not a partner.
- **Chat sidebar producing patches:** what the challenge says to avoid.
- **Tiptap / ProseMirror WYSIWYG:** the Markdown round-trip is lossy, and tracked changes over a node tree are notoriously hard.
- **Suggestion text inserted into the Document with marks:** the Markdown stays dirty while Suggestions are open, and Reject needs careful undo.

# 0002. Structured model output; the app owns the anchors

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q10, Q39

## Context

What can go wrong with a model's answer here:

| Failure | Plain text | Structured JSON |
|---|---|---|
| Wrapper chatter ("Sure! Here's…", code fences) | happens, needs cleaning | gone, the schema enforces the shape |
| Changes beyond the Instruction | happens | happens equally |
| Invented content | happens | happens equally |
| Wrong location (quotes text that doesn't exist) | impossible, the app knows the range | **new risk**, if the model picks the location |

The diff itself guards against rows 2 and 3: every change is visible before Accept. Structure removes row 1 and makes the answer checkable, but can create row 4.

## Decision

- **Strict structured outputs:** `structured_outputs` with OpenRouter `provider.require_parameters: true`, so only providers that support it are used. One zod schema per shape is both the validator and the source of the JSON Schema.
- **Target requests and Refine:** the app already knows the range. The model returns `{ replacement, rationale }`.
- **Review pass:** the app numbers Blocks (`p1`, `p2`, …) before sending. The model returns `{ edits: [{ blockId, replacement, rationale }] }` and never copies text to say where. A Block is a top-level node of the Markdown syntax tree; a whole list is one Block.
- **App-side validation:** drop an item when `replacement` equals the original or `blockId` is unknown. On invalid output, retry once silently, then show an error card.

## Consequences

- No chatter, a Rationale for every change, and answers the app can check.
- Review pass granularity is one Block: two changes in one paragraph become one Suggestion, and a long list is a single Suggestion.
- Format constraints may slightly lower writing quality ("Let Me Speak Freely?", 2024). The Bake-off watches for it ([0010](0010-model-bakeoff.md)).

## Alternatives considered

- **Plain-text Replacement for Target requests:** simplest, but no Rationale and no validation.
- **Quote-anchored edits `{ quote, replacement }` everywhere:** uniform, but a one-character slip in `quote` drops the edit, even where the app already knew the range.
- **Character offsets:** models are bad at counting characters.
- **Blank-line splitting for Blocks:** breaks on lists without blank lines and on code blocks that contain empty lines.

# 0003. Adaptive diff granularity

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q11

## Context

Word-level diffs are perfect for small fixes and unreadable "confetti" for rewrites. Block-level diffs are clear for rewrites and hide one-word fixes.

## Decision

Diff the original against the Replacement word by word (`diff`, `diffWords`). If the share of changed words exceeds a threshold (start at ~40%, calibrate on the sample Document), render block-level instead: the whole original struck through, the Replacement below it.

## Consequences

- Readable for both small fixes and rewrites.
- One threshold to tune, kept as a named constant with tests on both sides of it.

## Alternatives considered

- Always word-level.
- Always block-level.

# 0004. User-triggered AI, plus an on-demand Review pass

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q5, Q12, Q28

## Context

"The user is always in control", but the AI should feel like a co-author, not something that completes the whole Document.

## Decision

- **The AI acts only when asked.**
- **Selection bubble:** Quick actions (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar) plus a free-text "Ask AI…" field. `Cmd/Ctrl+K` opens the same field. With no selection, the Target is the Block under the cursor.
- **Review pass:** a toolbar button with an optional Focus. Without Focus, the AI looks at clarity, concision, grammar and tone consistency. It returns at most 6 Suggestions, most important first. It skips code blocks and Blocks that already have an open Suggestion.
- **No slash commands, no proactive hints.**
- Many Suggestions can be open at once from day one.

## Consequences

- Predictable, cheap, and the user is in control.
- The Review pass gives the "colleague marking up my draft" feeling without ambient noise.
- The 6-Suggestion cap leaves issues untouched in long, rough Documents. A wall of red and green would read as "the AI rewrote everything".

## Alternatives considered

- **Proactive hints on idle:** the strongest co-author feel, but it burns tokens under a US$5 cap, is noisy, and is hard to tune.
- **Slash commands:** they pull toward "generate at cursor", which is close to completing the Document.
- **Free-text only, no Quick actions:** less discoverable. Reviewers would have to invent what to ask.

# 0005. Local-only app; API key behind the Vite dev proxy

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q4, Q8, Q22

## Context

The challenge asks for "how to run it" and says no infrastructure is needed. The OpenRouter key has a US$5 cap and must not reach the browser.

## Decision

- **Run locally only:** `pnpm dev`. No deploy.
- **Proxy:** Vite `server.proxy` (and `preview.proxy`) forwards `/api/openrouter/*` to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` and overwrites `Authorization` with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from `.env`. The browser sends a placeholder key.
- **Missing-key banner:** `vite.config` exposes only a boolean, `__HAS_OPENROUTER_KEY__`, never the key. Without a key, a fixed banner explains what to set.
- **Config:** `.env.example` lists `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and an optional `OPENROUTER_MODEL`.

## Consequences

- No extra process to run, and the key never reaches the bundle.
- Prompts live in client code. They are not secret.
- Deploying later means replacing the proxy with a serverless function.

## Alternatives considered

- **Public deploy:** reviewers click a link, but anyone could spend the US$5, and it needs rate limiting and infrastructure.
- **Small Hono server with `/api/suggest`:** a second process and more code.
- **Key in the bundle (`VITE_OPENROUTER_KEY`):** leaks the key.

toolUseResult.content:
# 0006. Context window and prompt rules

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q18, Q26, Q27

## Context

A rewrite that ignores the surrounding tone feels pasted in. Sending the whole Document on every request costs more and invites the model to wander.

## Decision

- **Target requests and Refine:** send the Target, its Neighbors (2 Blocks before, 2 after, the document title and the current section heading, ~300–800 tokens), and the Instruction. Refine also sends the original text, previous Instructions and the latest Replacement.
- **Review pass:** send the whole Document with numbered Blocks (it must choose where to act).
- **Fixed prompt rules:**
  1. Answer in the Target's language.
  2. Change only what the Instruction needs.
  3. Do not invent facts, numbers or names.
  4. Preserve Markdown syntax (lists, links, emphasis).
  5. Rationale: one short sentence, in the Document's language.
- **Reasoning:** off or low for Quick actions, where the model allows it.

## Consequences

- Cheaper than sending the whole Document, and the Neighbors carry the tone.
- The model can miss consistency issues outside the Neighbors. That is what the Review pass is for.
- Rule 2 makes the AI timid on open Instructions like "make this better". Free text still allows big changes when the user asks for them.

## Alternatives considered

- **Target only:** cheapest, but blind to tone and topic.
- **Whole Document on every request:** best tone match, but more tokens. A size limit for huge Documents would also be needed (backlog).

toolUseResult.content:
# 0007. Suggestion lifecycle

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q13, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q25, Q32

## Context

Suggestions are overlays ([0001](0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md)) and the user keeps typing while they are open or in flight.

## Decision

- **Edits outside a Suggestion:** its range is mapped through the change (CodeMirror `ChangeSet` mapping).
- **Edits inside an open Suggestion, or inside an in-flight request's Target:** Discard it, with a discreet notice ("Suggestion discarded: the text changed").
- **Overlaps:** a new request over an open Suggestion replaces it, so the last one wins. The Review pass skips Blocks with open Suggestions.
- **Active Suggestion:** shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. Its Rationale shows on hover, and when the text cursor is inside it (keyboard users can't hover). Other Suggestions show only the inline diff.
- **Keys, with the cursor inside a Suggestion:** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` Accepts, `Esc` Rejects. Accept is a normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. Reject is not undoable in v1. A Review pass also offers Accept all and Reject all.
- **Refine:** a follow-up Instruction on the Active Suggestion. The new Replacement replaces the old one in place. The diff is always against the original text. History stays in memory, with no version arrows in v1.
- **Persistence:** only the Document text goes to `localStorage`. Open Suggestions are lost on reload.
- **Failures:**
  - Missing key: banner ([0005](0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
  - Failed call (network, `402` out of credit, `429`): the Suggestion becomes an error card with Retry. `402` gets its own message.
  - Invalid output: one silent retry, then the error card.
  - Timeout: 30 s.

## Consequences

- Simple, honest rules. A user who bumps into a Suggestion loses it, and can ask again.
- An accidental `Esc` loses a Suggestion. An undoable Reject is in the backlog.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep a stale Suggestion with "regenerate":** an extra state, and an old diff can't be drawn over changed text.
- **Lock the range while a Suggestion is open:** takes control away from the user.
- **Block new requests until the old Suggestion is resolved:** friction.
- **Allow overlapping Suggestions:** accepting one breaks the other.
- **Rationale always visible, or in a side panel:** the side panel drifts toward the chatbot sidebar.

toolUseResult.content:
# 0008. Stream only where each piece arrives validated

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q24, Q31

## Context

Streaming has three costs here: parsing half-finished JSON, a diff that jitters while text arrives (not-yet-rewritten original text shows as deleted), and showing text before it is validated.

AI SDK v7, verified in its docs on 2026-10-28:
- With `Output.object`, `partialOutputStream` yields partial objects that "cannot be validated against your provided schema". Only the final output is validated.
- With `Output.array`, `elementStream` yields each element "complete and validated against your element schema".

## Decision

- **Review pass:** stream with `Output.array` and `elementStream`. Each Suggestion appears once it is schema-validated by the SDK and checked by the app (`blockId` exists, Replacement differs from the original).
- **Target requests and Refine:** not streamed. `Output.object`, validated before anything is shown.
- **Reopen rule:** if the chosen model's median latency for Target requests is above ~3 s, add a Draft preview: streamed text without a diff that turns into the diff once validated.

## Consequences

- The slowest call, the Review pass, shows its first Suggestion early, with no validation trade-off.
- Target requests stay simple: one state, validated before display.
- The Draft preview sits in the backlog behind a measurable rule.

## Alternatives considered

- **No streaming at all:** simplest, but the Review pass waits for all 6 Suggestions.
- **Stream everything, including a Draft for Target requests:** matches the challenge's "live preview" idea, but adds a visual state and a Draft that can fail validation and vanish.

# 0009. AI SDK v7 instead of plain fetch

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q31 (web-verified on 2026-10-28)

## Context

Without streaming, plain `fetch` + zod was ~60–80 lines and fully transparent. With validated element streaming ([0008](0008-validated-streaming-only.md)) and per-call records ([AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md#ai-call-records)), the SDK pays for itself.

Facts at decision time:
- `ai@7.0.155` (7.0.0 released 2026-06-25) and `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@3.1.0`, which targets `ai@^7`. Both are ESM-only and require Node 22+.
- Telemetry in v7 is a pluggable integration (`registerTelemetry`). A custom integration receives lifecycle events (`onStart`, `onStepEnd` with `usage`, `onEnd`, …) without OpenTelemetry.
- Every OpenRouter response includes `usage` with `cost`, reasoning tokens and cached tokens. `GET /api/v1/generation?id=…` adds `latency`, `generation_time`, `provider_name`, native token counts and more.

## Decision

- Use `ai@^7` + `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@^3` + `zod`.
- The provider uses `baseURL` = `${location.origin}/api/openrouter` and a placeholder key. The proxy injects the real key.
- AI call records come from a custom `registerTelemetry` integration plus the generation endpoint.
- `scripts/bakeoff.ts` uses the same client in Node with the real key, so the Bake-off tests the code the app runs.
- Agents follow `.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk` and never write SDK code from memory.

## Consequences

- Element streaming with validation, lifecycle hooks for records, and a cheap path to Draft streaming later.
- Two more dependencies. Node 22+ goes in the README.
- Official recipes run the SDK on a server. We run it in the browser. The core uses `fetch`, and a Chrome article shows `streamText()` working in the browser.
- **Risk:** the provider README does not document `Output.object` or `json_schema`. Slice 2 must verify this. The fallback is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (not yet verified).

## Alternatives considered

- **Plain `fetch` + zod:** smallest and transparent, but no validated element streaming.
- **OpenTelemetry export:** from the browser it needs a vendor key in the bundle, or a server.
- **AI SDK DevTools:** stores data in a local JSON file, so it only works in Node. Usable for the Bake-off only.

# 0010. Choose the model by Bake-off

- Status: **Proposed**. Decided at Gate A ([docs/PLAN.md](../../PLAN.md#gates)).
- Source: planning session, Q23, Q33

## Context

On 2026-10-28, from OpenRouter's public API. Prices are US$ per million tokens. Cost per call assumes ~3k input and ~500 output tokens (a Review pass).

| Tier | Model | Origin | Input | Output | ~Cost/call | Providers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cheap | `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | US | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.0006 | 10 |
| Cheap | `openai/gpt-6-luna` | US | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.0006 | 7 |
| Cheap | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | CN | 0.14 | 0.42 | 0.0006 | 41 |
| Cheap | `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.50 | 0.0007 | 38 |
| Cheap | `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.47 | 0.0007 | 2 |
| Cheap | `minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.60 | 0.0008 | 13 |
| Cheap | `z-ai/glm-5.3` | CN | 0.07 | 1.40 | 0.0009 | 49 |
| Mid | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | US | 0.30 | 2.50 | 0.002 | 8 |
| Mid | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` | CN | 0.66 | 1.98 | 0.003 | 25 |
| Mid | `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | US | 0.83 | 4.13 | 0.005 | 7 |
| Mid | `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` | US | 1 | 5 | 0.006 | 4 |
| Top | `qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902` | CN | 2 | 6 | 0.009 | 2 |
| Top | `google/gemini-4-argon` | US | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 6 |
| Top | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` | US | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 8 |
| Top | `moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro` | CN | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 2 |

Notes:
- Every model listed supports `structured_outputs` on at least some providers (`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`: 32 of 38). `z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-prime` were excluded because they don't support it.
- Open-weight models are served by many providers with different quantization, so quality and latency depend on who serves the call. Pinning a provider trades away automatic fallback.
- OpenRouter's API returns `latency_last_30m: null`, so there is no speed data up front.
- Most of these models were released after the planning model's training data. Choosing from this table alone would be choosing by brand and price.

## Decision

`scripts/bakeoff.ts` runs the same requests against 9 models:

`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `google/gemini-3.8-flash`, `google/gemini-4-argon`, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

- **Requests:** the 4 Quick actions on fixed Targets of the sample Document, plus 1 Review pass.
- **Measured:** latency, cost, schema validity and retries, plus the outputs side by side. Written to `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`.
- **Choice:** the maintainer picks by reading the outputs. Tie-breakers, in order: Target-request latency under ~3 s, then cost. The result may be two models: a fast one for Target requests and a strong one for the Review pass.
- **Default:** configurable via `OPENROUTER_MODEL`.
- **Budget:** under US$0.50.

## Consequences

- The choice rests on evidence, not on a guess.
- About 30–40 minutes of work, plus a Gate.
- The Bake-off also verifies the `Output.object` risk from [0009](0009-ai-sdk-v7.md).

# Chiri AI Editor

A browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. Select text (or just place the cursor in a paragraph), ask for a change, and the AI proposes it inline as a tracked change: old text struck through, new text beside it, plus a one-line reason. # Implementation plan

Runbook for the implementation orchestrator. The planning session produced this plan, the [ADRs](chiri/adr/) and the issues below. Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and [GLOSSARY.md](../GLOSSARY.md) first.

## Roles

| Role | Model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `opus` | Runs the loop below, owns gates, merges PRs. Claude Code only, so every session log lands in `~/.claude/projects/`. |
| Implementer | `sonnet` subagent | One at a time, in the orchestrator's checkout, on the slice branch. |
| Reviewer, first pass | `opus` subagent, effort `medium` | Two axes, as in the `code-review` skill: **Standards** (against [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)) and **Spec** (against the issue and its ADRs). |
| Reviewer, later passes | `sonnet` subagent | Re-checks the fixes until no real findings remain. |

Slices run **sequentially**. Each builds on the previous one, and running them in parallel would collide on `package.json` and shared modules.

## Loop per slice

1. Branch from up-to-date `main`, using the name in the table below.
2. Implementer: TDD the pure modules the issue lists, then the UI.
3. Run the definition of done ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#definition-of-done-every-slice)): tests, Biome, build.
4. Verify the acceptance criteria in a real browser with `agent-browser`. Record the AI calls and screenshots ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#ai-call-records)) and update [chiri/ai-costs.md](chiri/ai-costs.md).
5. Open the PR with the `pr` skill and the [template](../.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).
6. First review (`opus`, medium), fix, then re-review (`sonnet`) until clean. Note the review outcome in the PR.
7. Squash merge.
8. If the slice ends at a gate, stop and wait.

## Slices

| # | Issue | Branch | Scope | Depends on | Gate after | Est. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #1 | `feat/editor-shell` | Vite + React + TS + Tailwind, CodeMirror with styled Markdown, sample Document, `localStorage`, proxy, missing-key banner, Biome, Vitest | — | — | 45 min |
| 2 | #2 | `feat/model-client-bakeoff` | AI SDK client, zod schemas, prompt building, Block extraction, AI call records, `scripts/bakeoff.ts`, `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md` | 1 | **A** | 60 min |
| 3 | #3 | `feat/selection-suggestions` | Selection bubble, `Cmd+K`, Quick actions, Suggestion state and mapping, adaptive diff, overlay decorations, Accept / Reject, Rationale, errors | 2, Gate A | **B** | 90 min |
| 4 | #4 | `feat/refine` | Refine on the Active Suggestion, history, diff against original | 3, Gate B | — | 30 min |
| 5 | #5 | `feat/review-pass` | Review pass with Focus, numbered Blocks, streamed validated Suggestions (max 6), skip occupied Blocks, Accept all / Reject all | 4 | — | 45 min |
| 6 | #6 | `docs/readme-and-sessions` | Final README, backlog review, session export script, `ai-sessions/` | 5 | **C** | 30 min |

That is about 5 h 15 of work, plus 30–40 min of reviews. If time runs short, shrink slice 5 first.

## Gates

- **A, after slice 2 (model):** present `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`, with outputs side by side, latency, cost and validity. The maintainer picks the model or models. Update [ADR 0010](chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md) to Accepted and set the default in `.env.example`. If any Target-request latency is above ~3 s, flag the Draft reopen rule ([ADR 0008](chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md)).
- **B, after slice 3 (core flow):** the maintainer tries select → Suggestion → Accept / Reject in the browser. Fix taste issues before Refine and the Review pass build on top.
- **C, before merging slice 6 (submission):** final look at the README, cost log, sessions and repo.

## Budget

US$5 OpenRouter cap. The Bake-off should stay under US$0.50. Every model call made during verification goes into [chiri/ai-costs.md](chiri/ai-costs.md). If the running total passes US$2, stop and tell the maintainer.

## Session logs (slice 6)

The challenge requires raw, unedited session files committed to the repo. Only secrets may be masked.

- Source: every folder in `~/.claude/projects/` whose name starts with `-home-walter-Github-chiri-ai-editor` (this covers every worktree). Copy each session's `<id>.jsonl` and its sibling `<id>/` folder (subagents, tool results) as they are. Skip non-session files such as `memory/`.
- Destination: `ai-sessions/<project-folder>/…`.
- Masking: replace OpenRouter keys (`sk-or-…`) with `sk-or-***MASKED***`, and nothing else.
- The script lives in `scripts/` and runs last, after the final PR text is written, so it captures as much as possible. Note in the README that the orchestrator session continues after the export.
- Claude Code deletes transcripts older than `cleanupPeriodDays`, 30 days by default. Export before then.

Base directory for this skill: /home/walter/.claude/skills/to-issues

# To Issues

Break a plan into independently-grabbable issues using vertical slices (tracer bullets).

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes an issue reference (issue number, URL, or path) as an argument, fetch it from the issue tracker and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Issue titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the plan into **tracer bullet** issues. Each issue is a thin vertical slice that cuts through ALL integration layers end-to-end, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer.

Slices may be 'HITL' or 'AFK'. HITL slices require human interaction, such as an architectural decision or a design review. AFK slices can be implemented and merged without human interaction. Prefer AFK over HITL where possible.

<vertical-slice-rules>
- Each slice delivers a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests)
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Prefer many thin slices over few thick ones
</vertical-slice-rules>

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each slice, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Type**: HITL / AFK
- **Blocked by**: which other slices (if any) must complete first
- **User stories covered**: which user stories this addresses (if the source material has them)

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)

## What to build

**Type:** AFK

Running `pnpm dev` opens a single-page app with a CodeMirror 6 editor showing raw Markdown with light styling (Obsidian-like), in a dark theme. On the first visit, the app loads a sample Document: English, ~250–400 words, with flaws planted for the AI to fix (an overlong sentence, a tone shift, a typo, a redundant passage, a list). A one-line hint says "Select text and press ⌘K". The Document autosaves to `localStorage` and comes back on reload.

The Vite dev proxy forwards `/api/openrouter/*` to OpenRouter and injects the key from `.env`. Without a key, a fixed banner explains what to set. Tooling is set up: pnpm, TypeScript strict, Tailwind v4 theme tokens, Biome, Vitest.

Decisions: [ADR 0001](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md), [ADR 0005](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md). Conventions: [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm install && pnpm dev` starts the app on Node 22+, with `packageManager` pinned.
- [ ] The editor renders raw Markdown with styled headings, emphasis, lists and code, in a dark theme. League Spartan is used for the app title only.
- [ ] The first visit shows the sample Document and the hint. Edits persist across reloads, and only the Document text is stored.
- [ ] `.env.example` lists `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and an optional `OPENROUTER_MODEL`.
- [ ] With a key, a browser request to `/api/openrouter/models` succeeds. The key value appears neither in the built bundle nor in browser-side request headers (placeholder only).
- [ ] Without a key, the missing-key banner shows (driven by a boolean `__HAS_OPENROUTER_KEY__`).
- [ ] `pnpm test` (at least one real test), `pnpm biome check` and `pnpm build` pass.
- [ ] Verified with `agent-browser`, with screenshots under `docs/chiri/verification/`.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

## What to build

**Type:** HITL. Ends at **Gate A**: the maintainer picks the model.

The AI layer the app will use, proven end to end against real models by a Bake-off script:

- **Block extraction:** top-level nodes of the Markdown syntax tree, a whole list is one Block, ids `p1…pn`.
- **Prompt building:**
  - Target requests: Target + Neighbors.
  - Refine inputs: original text, previous Instructions, latest Replacement.
  - Review pass: the whole Document with numbered Blocks and an optional Focus.
  - Always: the 5 fixed rules.
- **zod schemas:** `{ replacement, rationale }` and `{ edits: [{ blockId, replacement, rationale }] }`. Each schema is the single source for both validation and the JSON Schema sent to the model.
- **Model client:**
  - AI SDK v7 with `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider`. In the browser it points at the proxy; in Node it points at OpenRouter with the real key.
  - Strict structured outputs with `provider.require_parameters: true`.
  - One silent retry on invalid output and a 30 s timeout.
  - The Review pass streams through `Output.array` + `elementStream`.
- **AI call records:** fed by a custom `registerTelemetry` integration and enriched with `GET /api/v1/generation`.
- **`pnpm bakeoff`:** runs the 4 Quick actions on fixed Targets of the sample Document plus 1 Review pass against the 9 candidates in ADR 0010, and writes `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`.

Decisions: [0002](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0002-structured-output-app-owned-anchors.md), [0006](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md), [0008](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md), [0009](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0009-ai-sdk-v7.md), [0010](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md). Follow `.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk` and never write SDK code from memory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TDD covers Block extraction, prompt building, schema validation (including dropping items with an unknown `blockId` or a Replacement equal to the original), and AI call record shaping. Tests never call the real model.
- [ ] Confirmed that `Output.object` / `Output.array` with the OpenRouter provider sends a strict JSON schema. If they don't, switch to the fallback and update ADR 0009.
- [ ] The Review pass streams validated elements and records time to the first element.
- [ ] Reasoning is off or low for Quick actions where the model allows it.
- [ ] `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md` shows, per model: latency, cost, validity and retries, plus the outputs side by side.
- [ ] The total Bake-off cost is under US$0.50, and its rows are added to `docs/chiri/ai-costs.md`.
- [ ] **Gate A:** the orchestrator presents `bakeoff.md` and waits. After the choice, ADR 0010 is set to Accepted and the default model goes into `.env.example`.

## Blocked by

- #1

## What to build

**Type:** HITL. Ends at **Gate B**: the maintainer tries the core flow.

The core co-author loop.

- **Asking:**
  - Selecting text shows a floating bubble with Quick actions (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar) and an "Ask AI…" field. `⌘/Ctrl+K` opens the same field.
  - With no selection, the Target is the Block under the cursor.
  - The Target shimmers while waiting.
- **Showing:**
  - The Suggestion renders inline as an overlay with an adaptive diff: word-level, or block-level when more than ~40% changed.
  - The Active Suggestion shows Accept / Reject. Refine is added in the next slice.
  - The Rationale shows on hover and when the text cursor is inside the Suggestion.
- **Resolving:** `⌘/Ctrl+Enter` Accepts (undoable with `⌘Z`), and `Esc` Rejects.
- **Editing around Suggestions:**
  - Edits outside a Suggestion keep it aligned.
  - Edits inside an open Suggestion, or inside an in-flight Target, Discard it with a notice.
  - A new request overlapping an open Suggestion replaces it.
  - Many Suggestions can be open at once.
- **Errors:**
  - A failed call becomes an error card with Retry. `402` gets an "out of credit" message.
  - Invalid output is retried once silently, then shows the error card.

Decisions: [0001](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md), [0003](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0003-adaptive-diff.md), [0004](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0004-user-triggered-ai-and-review-pass.md), [0007](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TDD covers the adaptive diff (cases on both sides of the threshold), Suggestion state transitions (create, Accept, Reject, Discard, replace on overlap), and position mapping for edits outside and inside a Suggestion.
- [ ] Each Quick action and a free-text Instruction produce a Suggestion on the sample Document with the model chosen at Gate A.
- [ ] `⌘K` with no selection targets the Block under the cursor.
- [ ] Accept applies the Replacement and `⌘Z` restores the original. Reject leaves the Document unchanged.
- [ ] Typing inside an open Suggestion Discards it with a notice. Typing elsewhere keeps it aligned.
- [ ] The Rationale is visible on hover and with the cursor inside.
- [ ] A forced failure (for example a bad key or a mocked `402`) shows the error card with Retry.
- [ ] AI call records and screenshots are in `docs/chiri/verification/`, and `docs/chiri/ai-costs.md` is updated.
- [ ] **Gate B:** the orchestrator asks the maintainer to try the flow and waits.

## Blocked by

- #2

## What to build

**Type:** AFK

Running `pnpm dev` opens a single-page app with a CodeMirror 6 editor showing raw Markdown with light styling (Obsidian-like), in a dark theme. The Vite dev proxy forwards `/api/openrouter/*` to OpenRouter and injects the key from `.env`. Without a key, a fixed banner explains what to set. Tooling is set up: pnpm, TypeScript strict, Tailwind v4 theme tokens, Biome, Vitest.

Decisions: [ADR 0001](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md), [ADR 0005](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md). - [ ] The first visit shows the sample Document and the hint. Edits persist across reloads, and only the Document text is stored.
- [ ] `.env.example` lists `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and an optional `OPENROUTER_MODEL`.

- [ ] **Gate B:** the orchestrator asks the maintainer to try the flow and waits.

## Blocked by

- #2

## What to build

**Type:** AFK

The Active Suggestion's toolbar gains **Refine**: a small input for follow-ups like "make it shorter" or "now more formal". The model receives the original text, the Neighbors, the previous Instructions and the latest Replacement. It returns a new `{ replacement, rationale }`, which replaces the Suggestion in place. The diff is always against the original text. History stays in memory, with no version arrows (backlog). The Discard rules still apply.

Decisions: [0006](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md), [0007](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TDD covers the Refine prompt (original text, Instruction history, latest Replacement) and the Suggestion history update.
- [ ] Two consecutive Refines on the same Suggestion each update it in place, and the diff stays against the original text.
- [ ] Accept after Refine applies the latest Replacement.
- [ ] A failed Refine shows Retry without losing the current Replacement.
- [ ] AI call records and screenshots are in `docs/chiri/verification/`, and `docs/chiri/ai-costs.md` is updated.

## Blocked by

- #3

## What to build

**Type:** AFK

A **Review** button in the toolbar opens an optional Focus field. The app sends the whole Document with numbered Blocks. Without a Focus, the AI looks at clarity, concision, grammar and tone consistency.

The model returns at most 6 edits, streamed through `Output.array` + `elementStream`, most important first. Each validated element becomes a Suggestion on its Block as soon as it arrives, with the adaptive diff and a Rationale. Code blocks and Blocks that already have an open Suggestion are skipped. While review Suggestions are open, Accept all and Reject all are available, and each Suggestion can still be resolved on its own.

Decisions: [0002](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0002-structured-output-app-owned-anchors.md), [0004](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0004-user-triggered-ai-and-review-pass.md), [0007](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md), [0008](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TDD covers mapping edits to Suggestions: an unknown `blockId` is dropped, an unchanged Replacement is dropped, occupied Blocks and code blocks are skipped, and there are at most 6.
- [ ] On the sample Document, the first Suggestion appears before the stream ends, and the time to the first Suggestion is recorded.
- [ ] A Focus visibly changes the kind of Suggestions returned.
- [ ] Accept all and Reject all work, and single Accept / Reject / Refine still work on review Suggestions.
- [ ] AI call records and screenshots are in `docs/chiri/verification/`, and `docs/chiri/ai-costs.md` is updated.

When this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, it also holds one short question, the decision alone with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give, plus buttons of one to three words that answer it; a turn with nothing pending sends the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Your closing message follows the call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the box's recap never replaces. Never write it before the call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The call's result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR the app watches it and wakes you on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments, so the box never offers to keep watching, poll or fix CI, in a question or a button. It asks only what the user must do or decide (an approval, a review request, a choice), as one question. Part of wrapping up is deciding, unasked, whether what the user asked for left a real follow-up, and where it runs; most turns leave none. One piece of work that acts on what this session just found stays here while this session has nothing else in flight ("Starting other sessions" says why): make it the box's question, with a button that has you do it here. A piece you left or could not verify is still this task, not a follow-up: finish or check it now, here or in a subagent, or name it in the recap. Any other that is a task of its own, as that section defines one (work that lands apart from this change, something the user set aside earlier, or a self-contained next task better started fresh than from a long history — never work unrelated to the request), you propose with `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` (initiation "own_initiative"; skip if you already did this turn); it shows as a New task card in the transcript, where the user starts it.

<browsers>
You have two browsers in this session:
- The built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser": a browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the user's Chrome. The built-in browser is the default for this session and its tools are already loaded, so use it unless the user asks for Claude in Chrome.
